Candidate 23 passes as supplied. The artwork maps confidently to the numbered routing: Hole 1 is the long upper fairway beside the lake, Hole 2 is the island green near T3, and Hole 3 is the dry dogleg returning across the lower property. The 5:3 canvas, compact irregular shared property, folded routing, varied orientations, nearby G1/T2 and G2/T3 connections, grassy breaks, and continuous interior grass all read clearly. The putting surfaces appear as single natural light-green areas with restrained fringes, not nested discs or raised platforms.

Hole 1 is a 483-yard reachable par 5 with one substantial lake alongside the fairway and a usable landing corridor. The artwork preserves the lake's extent and the bunker relationships. Favoring the dry side offers a sensible staged route; pushing closer to the shoreline can improve position for an attempt to reach in two. Hole 2 is a 176-yard island-green par 3 with a substantial surrounding lake and a separate approach bunker. The illustration retains the island proportions and bunker placement. This is chiefly a carry and distance-control test, with center-green play offering a safer target than a pin attack. Hole 3 is a dry 371-yard dogleg-left par 4. The bent fairway and greenside bunker group are recognizable, and the broad route gives a conservative alternative to challenging the turn. Its simulated one-shot reach is an opportunity, not evidence that the direct line is reliably easy.

The par-5/3/4 sequence, one dry hole, island carry, and contrasting dogleg provide excellent variety within the round. Island greens and reachable par 5s recur in the recent history, but the dry dogleg finish and this combination distinguish the round sufficiently from the latest publication. Simulated shots-to-green of 2/1/1 and 55/44/55 safe tee options support a testing but playable design; the previews also show credible landing areas and targets. No clear artwork mismatch or safe geometry correction warrants an edit.
